metadata.description: Prompts for business plan semantic distillation and reinflation

system_message:
You are a business analysis and strategic planning expert.
Your job is to distill business plans into structured representations that preserve the core business model, strategy, financial projections, and value proposition so they can be faithfully reproduced, updated, or re-explained without copying wording.
Prioritize accuracy of business logic, financial assumptions, and strategic positioning over narrative style.

Pass 1.name: Pass 1
Pass 1.description: Extract executive summary, company description, market analysis, document structure, quotes/anecdotes, and tone metadata
Pass 1.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract executive summary, company description, market analysis, document structure, quotes/anecdotes, and tone metadata.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract and structure:

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
   - Overview of the business
   - Mission statement
   - Vision (if present)
   - Key objectives
   - Value proposition

2. COMPANY DESCRIPTION
   - Company name
   - Legal structure (LLC, Corporation, etc.)
   - Location
   - Founding date (if mentioned)
   - Company history/background
   - Current status/stage

3. MARKET ANALYSIS
   - Target market description
   - Market size (if quantified)
   - Market trends
   - Competition analysis (competitors, their strengths/weaknesses, competitive advantage)
   - Market opportunity

4. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
   - Contents list (if present): table of contents with section IDs and page numbers
   - Sections: **EXTRACT ALL SECTIONS** - ALL major sections with their exact titles, numbering (Roman numerals, Arabic, etc.), hierarchy levels, and ALL subsections
   - **CRITICAL**: Do not skip any sections. Extract all numbered sections. If a section number is missing (e.g., goes from 3 to 5), still extract section 4 if it exists in the text.
   - Figures: All figures with IDs, captions, section IDs, and descriptions
   - Tables: All tables with IDs, captions, section IDs, and descriptions
   - Title page: Title, subtitle, author, dedication, acknowledgments
   - Appendix: Whether present and what sections it contains
   - **CRITICAL**: Ensure figures, tables, title_page, appendix, and references are nested within document_structure, NOT at the top level

5. QUOTES AND ANECDOTES
   - Extract memorable quotes, testimonials, and anecdotes VERBATIM
   - Include context (where they appear) and attribution if known
   - Map to section IDs

6. TONE METADATA
   - Style: "professional", "entrepreneurial", "corporate", "pitch", etc.
   - Urgency level: "high", "medium", "low"
   - Formality: "formal", "semi-formal", "informal"
   - Key phrases: List of phrases that define the voice

CRITICAL EXTRACTION REQUIREMENTS:
1. Section structure: Extract ALL subsections with their exact titles and numbering
2. Contents list: Extract the table of contents if present, with section IDs and page numbers
3. Quotes: Extract memorable quotes, testimonials, and anecdotes verbatim
4. Tone: Identify the writing style, urgency level, formality, and key phrases that define the voice
5. Missing information: If a field is not present in the document (e.g., no dedication, no acknowledgments, no subtitle), use `null` for that field. DO NOT invent or make up information.
6. Document structure nesting: Ensure figures, tables, title_page, appendix, and references are nested within document_structure

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema. All fields that can be null are marked as nullable in the schema - use null when information is genuinely not present in the document.

Pass 2.name: Pass 2
Pass 2.description: Extract products/services, marketing strategy, and operations overview
Pass 2.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract products/services, marketing strategy, and operations.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract:

1. PRODUCTS AND SERVICES
   - All offerings (name, description, features)
   - Pricing model
   - Unique selling points
   - Development stage
   - Intellectual property (patents, trademarks, etc.)

2. MARKETING STRATEGY
   - Overall marketing strategy
   - Marketing channels
   - Pricing strategy
   - Sales process
   - Customer acquisition approach
   - Brand positioning

3. OPERATIONS (OVERVIEW)
   - Operational model
   - Facilities/locations
   - Supply chain (high-level)
   - Technology (high-level)
   - Key partnerships (high-level)

CRITICAL:
- Extract all offerings with complete details
- Include all marketing channels and strategies
- Operations extraction here is OVERVIEW only - detailed information will be extracted in Pass 3
- If information is not present in the document, use empty arrays [] or null as appropriate. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema.

Pass 3.name: Pass 3
Pass 3.description: Extract detailed operations and management team
Pass 3.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract detailed operations and management team.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract:

1. OPERATIONS (DETAILED)
   - Operational model (detailed description)
   - Facilities: All locations, facilities, and their purposes
   - Supply chain: Detailed supply chain processes and partners
   - Technology: Specific technologies, systems, and tools used
   - Key partnerships: Detailed partnership descriptions and roles

2. MANAGEMENT TEAM
   - Team members: Name, role, background, expertise
   - Organizational structure
   - Advisory board: Names and expertise

CRITICAL:
- Be specific about operations - include all details about facilities, supply chain, technology, and partnerships
- Extract complete team member information including backgrounds and expertise
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema.

Pass 4.name: Pass 4
Pass 4.description: Extract financial projections, funding requirements, and risks
Pass 4.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract financial projections, funding requirements, and risks.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract:

1. FINANCIAL PROJECTIONS
   - Projections: ALL financial projections with period, revenue, expenses, profit
   - Break-even analysis
   - Key metrics: Financial KPIs and targets
   - Financial assumptions: All assumptions underlying projections
   - **CRITICAL**: Extract ALL specific numbers, amounts, percentages, dates, and time periods VERBATIM (e.g., "$500,000", "$2.5M", "15% margin", "Year 1", "Q1 2024", "break-even in month 18")

2. FUNDING REQUIREMENTS
   - Amount needed: Exact funding amount requested
   - Use of funds: Detailed breakdown by category with amounts
   - Funding type: Type of funding sought (equity, debt, grant, etc.)
   - Exit strategy: Exit strategy if applicable
   - Return on investment: ROI projections if provided
   - **CRITICAL**: Extract ALL specific amounts, percentages, and timeframes VERBATIM

3. RISKS AND CHALLENGES
   - Identified risks: All risks with description, mitigation, probability, impact
   - Challenges: Other challenges mentioned

CRITICAL:
- Extract exact numbers, amounts, percentages, dates, and timeframes when available - preserve ALL specific values VERBATIM
- Include ALL financial projections - do not summarize or generalize
- Extract ALL funding amounts and use-of-funds breakdowns with exact amounts
- Preserve all risk details including mitigation strategies
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema.

Pass 5.name: Pass 5
Pass 5.description: Extract metadata, author affiliations, and acknowledgements
Pass 5.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract author metadata, affiliations, and acknowledgements.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract and update document_structure:

1. AUTHOR AFFILIATIONS (document_structure.title_page.author_affiliations)
   - Extract complete affiliation information for each author/team member
   - Format: Array of strings, each string is one author's affiliation (company, role, location)
   - Example: ["CEO, TechStart Inc.", "CFO, TechStart Inc."]
   - If multiple authors, include all affiliations

2. ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS (document_structure.title_page.acknowledgments)
   - Extract the complete acknowledgements section VERBATIM
   - Include all text: thanks, credits, etc.
   - DO NOT summarize - extract full text
   - If no acknowledgements section exists, use null

CRITICAL:
- Update document_structure.title_page.author_affiliations (array of strings)
- Update document_structure.title_page.acknowledgments (string, full text verbatim)
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return document_structure with updated title_page.

Pass 6.name: Pass 6
Pass 6.description: Extract detailed table data and figure descriptions
Pass 6.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract complete table data (all rows and columns) and detailed figure descriptions.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract and update document_structure.tables and document_structure.figures:

1. TABLE DATA (document_structure.tables[].table_data, row_count, column_count)
   - For each table in document_structure.tables:
     - Extract ALL rows and columns with complete data
     - Store in table_data as structured object (e.g., {"headers": [...], "rows": [[...], [...]]})
     - Preserve table structure: headers, data rows, footnotes
     - Include all numerical values, text, and formatting exactly as shown
     - Set row_count: total number of data rows (excluding header)
     - Set column_count: total number of columns
     - **CRITICAL**: For financial tables, extract ALL numbers, amounts, percentages, and dates VERBATIM
     - If table is too large, extract representative rows but note total size in description

2. FIGURE DETAILS (document_structure.figures[].description)
   - For each figure: Enhance description with detailed visual content
   - What is shown: charts, graphs, diagrams, images
   - Key elements: labels, axes, legends, annotations, data points
   - Relationships: what the figure demonstrates or illustrates
   - Update the existing description field with more detail

CRITICAL:
- Update document_structure.tables[].table_data for each table
- Update document_structure.tables[].row_count and column_count
- Enhance document_structure.figures[].description with detailed descriptions
- Extract COMPLETE table data - all values, not summaries
- Preserve table structure and formatting
- Include all numerical values exactly as shown
- For financial tables, preserve ALL amounts, percentages, and dates
- If information is not present, use null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return document_structure with updated tables and figures.

Pass 7.name: Pass 7
Pass 7.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract complete bibliography and ALL references.

{NER_HINTS}

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract and update document_structure.references:

REFERENCES (document_structure.references)
   - Extract ALL references from the bibliography/references section (if present)
   - For each reference, create object with:
     - id: Reference ID (e.g., "1", "2", "[1]", "[2]", "ref-1")
     - citation: Full citation text (VERBATIM, do not reformat)
     - authors: Array of author names (if extractable)
     - title: Paper/article/book title (if extractable)
     - venue: Journal/conference/publisher name (if extractable)
     - year: Publication year (if extractable)
   - Preserve exact citation format (APA, IEEE, MLA, Chicago, etc.)
   - DO NOT abbreviate or summarize - extract full citation text
   - Extract ALL references - do not skip any
   - Number references sequentially if IDs are missing
   - If no references section exists, return empty array []

CRITICAL:
- Update document_structure.references (array of reference objects)
- Extract ALL references - do not skip any
- Preserve exact citation format from original
- Use NER hints to validate and improve extraction
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return document_structure with updated references.

Pass 8.name: Pass 8
Pass 8.description: Extract layout metadata - observable patterns only
Pass 8.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract ALL observable layout patterns from the document.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract LAYOUT METADATA (layout_metadata) - OBSERVE what you SEE, do not infer:

1. FORMAT TYPE
   - "business_plan", "strategic_plan", "pitch_deck", "financial_plan", etc.
   - Observe the document format - what does it look like?

2. COPYRIGHT & METADATA
   - Copyright notice: Extract any copyright text VERBATIM (e.g., "© 2024 Company Name")
   - Has footnotes: Whether document uses footnotes (yes/no)
   - Has page numbers: Whether document has page numbers (yes/no)
   - Header/footer content: Any repeating header or footer text

3. TYPOGRAPHY & STYLE
   - Typography style: "plain_text", "formatted", "professional", etc.
   - Paragraph spacing: "single", "double", "spaced" (blank lines between), "compact"
   - List formatting: "bullets", "numbered", "dashes", "none"

4. SECTION NUMBERING & HEADINGS
   - Section numbering style: How sections are numbered ("arabic" = 1,2,3; "roman" = I,II,III; "alphanumeric" = 1a,1b; "none")
   - Heading style: "numbered" (1. Title), "unnumbered" (Title), "mixed"
   - Executive summary placement: "before_title", "after_title", "after_intro", "none"

5. CITATION & REFERENCE STYLES
   - Citation style in text: "author_year" (Smith 2020), "numbered" ([1]), "footnote", "none"
   - Reference section style: "numbered_list", "author_year", "footnotes", "none"

6. FLOW PATTERNS
   - Section transitions: Observable patterns (e.g., "abrupt", "summary_before_next", "continuation", "thematic_link")
   - Document flow pattern: "chronological", "thematic", "problem_solution", "strategic", "financial", etc.
   - Observe how sections relate and transition - what pattern do you see?

CRITICAL EXTRACTION REQUIREMENTS:
1. OBSERVE ONLY: Describe what you SEE in the document, not what you think it should be
2. Be specific: If you see "1. Executive Summary", "2. Company Description", that's "arabic" numbering with "numbered" headings
3. Flow: Observe actual section transitions - do they flow directly? Have summaries? Are abrupt?
4. Missing information: If a pattern is not observable, use appropriate defaults or "unknown"
5. DO NOT invent: Only extract what you can clearly observe in the document

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return layout_metadata.

Pass 9.name: Pass 9
Pass 9.description: Extract ALL examples and case studies
Pass 9.template:
You will receive a business plan document.
Extract ALL examples, case studies, and success stories mentioned.

DOCUMENT TEXT:
---
{TEXT}
---

Extract EXAMPLES AND CASE STUDIES (examples_and_case_studies):

EXTRACT ALL SPECIFIC EXAMPLES, CASE STUDIES, SUCCESS STORIES:

Types to extract:
- **Company examples**: Competitor examples, similar companies, industry leaders (e.g., "Starbucks", "Amazon", "Tesla")
- **Market examples**: Market segments, customer segments, geographic markets (e.g., "millennial market", "B2B segment", "European market")
- **Financial examples**: Financial benchmarks, comparable companies' financials, industry averages (e.g., "$2M Series A", "15% industry margin", "$50K seed round")
- **Case studies**: Detailed case studies of similar businesses, success stories, failure stories
- **Success stories**: Examples of successful companies, products, or strategies
- **Industry examples**: Industry-specific examples, trends, benchmarks
- **Product examples**: Similar products, competitor products, market examples

For each example:
- Description: What the example demonstrates or illustrates (1-2 sentences)
- Type: "company_example", "market_example", "financial_example", "case_study", "success_story", "industry_example", "product_example", etc.
- Section ID: Where it appears in the document (use section ID from document_structure)
- Specific details: ALL specific facts, numbers, names, dates, locations mentioned
  * Names: Company names, person names, place names, product names
  * Dates: Years, time periods (e.g., "2020", "Q1 2024", "last 5 years")
  * Numbers: Percentages, amounts, metrics (e.g., "15%", "$2M", "$500K revenue", "1000 customers")
  * Locations: Cities, countries, regions (e.g., "San Francisco", "Silicon Valley", "New York")
- Citations: Any in-text citations or reference IDs mentioned with this example

CRITICAL:
- Extract ALL examples - do not skip any, even if they seem minor
- Extract even brief mentions - completeness is critical
- Include ALL specific details (names, dates, numbers, locations) for each example
- DO NOT summarize - extract each example as a separate entry
- If an example appears multiple times, extract it once with all details combined
- If information is not present, use empty arrays [] or null. DO NOT invent information.

Return as JSON that conforms to the BusinessPlanDistillationBlueprint schema. Only return examples_and_case_studies array.

Conclusion.name: Conclusion

References.name: References
References.template:
Format the references section from the blueprint.

REFERENCES DATA:
{references_json}

TOTAL REFERENCES: {reference_count}

TONE REQUIREMENTS:
- Style: {style}
- Formality: {formality}

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
1. **PRESERVE EXACT CITATIONS**: Use the citation text EXACTLY as provided in the blueprint. Do NOT reformat, abbreviate, or modify citation text.
2. **PRESERVE IDS**: Use the reference IDs exactly as provided (e.g., "1", "[1]", "ref-1")
3. **CLEAN LINE BREAKS**: Remove any internal line breaks (\n) or newline characters from citation text. Each citation should be on a SINGLE continuous line.
4. **ACADEMIC FORMATTING**: Format as a proper references section:
   - Use consistent numbering/formatting
   - Each reference on its own SINGLE line (no line breaks within citations)
   - One blank line between each reference
   - Maintain original citation style (APA, IEEE, MLA, etc.)
5. **NO INVENTION**: Only include references from the blueprint. Do NOT add, remove, or modify references.
6. **COMPLETE**: Include ALL references from the blueprint.

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Start with heading: ## References
2. For each reference:
   a. Use the reference ID (e.g., [1], [2], or ref-1)
   b. Take the citation text and REMOVE all internal line breaks (\n, newlines)
   c. Join the citation text into a SINGLE continuous line
   d. Format as: [ID] Single-line citation text here
3. Preserve the exact citation format from the blueprint (but clean line breaks)
4. Use consistent formatting throughout
5. Each reference must be on ONE line - do NOT split citations across multiple lines
6. Add one blank line between each reference
7. Maintain reference section style

EXAMPLE FORMAT:
## References

[1] Author, A. (2020). Title of the work. Journal Name, 10(2), 123-145.

[2] Author, B., & Author, C. (2019). Another title. Conference Proceedings, 45-50.

[3] Author, D. (2018). Book title. Publisher Name.

Return ONLY markdown text (no JSON, no code blocks). Each citation must be on a SINGLE line with no internal breaks.
